questions.q: What is Bachata Sensual?
questions.a: Bachata Sensual is a modern and expressive style of bachata created in Spain by Korke and Judith. It is characterized by soft, fluid movements such as body waves and isolations, with a strong focus on musical interpretation and close connection between dance partners. The goal is not just to execute steps, but to use the whole body to visually express the emotions and nuances of the music.

questions.q: I have never danced before – are your courses suitable for me?
questions.a: Absolutely! Our beginner courses are designed for those who have never taken a dance step before. We guide you step by step.

questions.q: Are the courses open to all ages?
questions.a: Yes! We have students ranging from 18 to 60+. Everyone is welcome!

questions.q: Do you offer private lessons?
questions.a: Yes! You can book private lessons with our instructors, which is perfect if you want to progress faster or focus on specific details. Go to the 'Instructors' tab to read more and contact the instructor you are interested in booking.

questions.q: Do I need to bring a partner?
questions.a: No! You can come alone. We rotate partners during class so that everyone gets to dance with everyone.

questions.q: What happens if there is an uneven number of leaders and followers?
questions.a: We do our best to balance the groups. Sometimes you may have to wait a rotation, but we often have assistant instructors who step in to help.

questions.q: What should I wear?
questions.a: Comfortable clothes that allow you to move freely. Sneakers or dance shoes with a smooth sole work well – there is no requirement for special shoes.

questions.q: How long is each course?
questions.a: Right now we are running a workshop in weeks 49 and 50. Each level is 2 weeks, Monday to Thursday at 18:30–20:30.

questions.q: Do you offer drop-in classes?
questions.a: Not for our courses, where you sign up for the full period. Sunday Social Dance on Sundays 15:00–18:00 is bought as a single session for 80 SEK, and members get 50% off.

questions.q: Can I make up a missed lesson?
questions.a: Yes, if there is space in another group at the same level, you can jump in there for that week. Contact us and we will help you.

questions.q: How much do the courses cost?
questions.a: The workshop in weeks 49 and 50 costs 500 SEK for 2 weeks. Couples pay 900 SEK. Students get a 10% discount.

questions.q: Do you sell gift cards?
questions.a: Yes. A gift card is a balance you choose yourself: 1,000, 2,000 or 3,000 SEK, or your own amount. Learn more and buy via Gift card (fuegodanceschool.se/en/gift-card).

questions.q: I am a student – do I get a discount?
questions.a: Yes! We offer a 10% discount for students upon presentation of a valid student ID.

questions.q: Do you have a couple discount?
questions.a: Yes. Couples pay 900 SEK for 2 weeks, instead of 500 SEK per person.

questions.q: I can only attend every other week – do I get a discount?
questions.a: The every-other-week discount does not apply to the workshop in weeks 49 and 50. It is 2 weeks at a fixed price: 500 SEK, or 900 SEK for a couple.

questions.q: Can discounts be combined?
questions.a: No, discounts cannot unfortunately be combined. You choose the discount that suits you best.

questions.q: How do I sign up?
questions.a: You can sign up in two ways: 1) Go to our 'Schedule' page and click 'Book now'. 2) Go to the 'Our Courses' page for details and book from there.

questions.q: How do I sign up for the open house?
questions.a: You sign up via the 'Sign up for Open House' button found at the top of the homepage. IMPORTANT: Registration does not guarantee a spot, it is 'first come, first served'.

questions.q: Can I sign up for multiple courses?
questions.a: Absolutely! You can easily select multiple courses in the registration form.

questions.q: Can I cancel my payment?
questions.a: Yes, according to the Distance Contracts Act, you have a 14-day right of withdrawal from the purchase, provided the course has not started. If the course has begun or if you participated in the first trial lesson, the right of withdrawal does not apply.
